test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: After selling an article at a discount of 4%, the profit percentage obtained is 20%. What is the markup percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio: CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 4) : (100 + 20)

CP : MP = 96 : 120 = 4 : 5

Markup = 5 − 4 = 1 unit on CP of 4 units

Markup percentage = 1/4 = 0.25

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Discount = 4%, Profit = 20%

Formula: Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit%) and SP = MP × (1 − Discount%)

 CP (100) SP (120) MP (125) 
 +20% Profit 
 −4% Discount Markup = MP − CP = 25 

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

⇒ Profit = 20% ⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 20 = 120

⇒ Discount = 4% on Marked Price (MP) ⇒ SP = 96% of MP

⇒ 0.96 × MP = 120

⇒ MP = 120 / 0.96 = 125

⇒ Markup = MP − CP = 125 − 100 = 25

⇒ Markup percentage = 25 / 100 = 0.25

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discount Formula

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the total discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂/100)%.

Markup Percentage

Markup percentage is calculated on the Cost Price: Markup% = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.
